eyebrow: Quantum Error Correction & Fault Tolerance · Chapter 6
subtitle: Lesson 25 · Logical vs. Physical Qubits & Resource Estimation

steps.label: There exists a threshold physical error rate, p_th
steps.sub: Below it, increasing distance d suppresses logical error exponentially

steps.label: At or above p_th, increasing d does not help
steps.sub: And can actively make the logical error rate worse

steps.label: A well-established, proven theoretical result
steps.sub: The mathematical reason scalable quantum computation is possible in principle

eyebrow: Illustrative scaling: p_th = 0.01, p = 0.001 (p is 1/10th of threshold)
caption: d=7 to d=15 costs ~4.6x more qubits (449/97) but buys ~10,000x better suppression (1e-8 vs 1e-4) — a genuinely favorable trade.

eyebrow: The asymmetry above threshold, and what's proven vs. empirical

steps.label: At or above p_th, (p/p_th) ≥ 1
steps.sub: Raising it to a higher power keeps the result flat or grows it

steps.label: More physical qubits above threshold means more chances to fail
steps.sub: Without the exponential suppression available to compensate

steps.label: The theorem's existence is proven; the real p_th value isn't
steps.sub: Whether a given real device sits below it is empirical, hardware-specific, still evolving

subtitle: Put this math to work on an actual question: how many qubits to run Shor's algorithm at scale.
